html:
Peace deal signed in Belfast on 10 April 1998 that ended most of the violence of the-troubles in Northern Ireland.

It was reached after talks chaired by the US senator George Mitchell, with Tony Blair for Britain and Bertie Ahern for Ireland. Most Northern Irish parties took part, including Sinn Fein. The terms set up a new Northern Ireland Assembly with power shared between unionists and nationalists, links between north and south, release of paramilitary prisoners, and a plan to give up weapons. Ireland dropped its constitutional claim to the whole island. Northern Ireland would stay in the United Kingdom as long as most of its people wished.

In May 1998, about 71 percent in Northern Ireland and 94 percent in the Republic voted yes. The deal came after the ceasefires of the Provisional IRA and was often tested, but large-scale killing largely stopped.
sum: Peace deal signed in Belfast on 10 April 1998 that ended most of the violence of the-troubles in Northern Ireland.
